title: Standard method demand load
requirement: General lighting starts at 3 VA/sq ft (33 VA/m²) and takes the 220.42 demand tiers: first 3,000 VA at 100%, the next 117,000 VA at 35%, the remainder at 25%. Four or more appliance loads may take 75%, and heating and cooling are taken at the larger, not both.

title: Optional method for a dwelling
requirement: For a dwelling unit the optional method takes 100% of the first 10 kVA and 40% of the rest of the general and appliance load, then adds the 220.82(C) heating, cooling, range and dryer loads at their listed percentages.

title: Service rating from the calculated load
requirement: The service rating must carry the calculated load, and a single-family dwelling service may not be smaller than 100 A (3-wire, 120/240 V).

title: Service disconnecting means
requirement: The service needs a disconnecting means at a readily accessible point nearest the entry of the conductors, marked as the service disconnect, with no more than six service disconnects in one enclosure.

title: Panelboard spaces and directory
requirement: Every circuit needs a permanent directory, and the panelboard must have enough spaces for the circuits plus the spare capacity the code and good practice expect.

title: Working space at the panel
requirement: Provide at least 30 in of width, 36 in of depth and 6 ft 6 in of height of clear working space in front of the panel, with the panel door able to open 90°.

title: Conductor ampacity and the 60 °C limit
requirement: Conductors are sized from Table 310.16 for the termination temperature, and NM-B cable is limited to the 60 °C column.

title: Ambient and conductor-count adjustment
requirement: Ampacity is adjusted for ambient temperature and for more than three current-carrying conductors in a raceway: 80% for 4–6, 70% for 7–9 and 50% for 10–20.

title: Raceway fill
requirement: One conductor may fill 53% of a raceway, two 31%, and three or more 40% of the interior cross-sectional area.

title: Box fill
requirement: Each box must have enough volume for its conductors, devices, clamps and grounds: 2.0 in³ per 14 AWG, 2.25 per 12 AWG, 2.5 per 10 AWG, plus two allowances per device and one for the grounds.

title: Voltage drop
requirement: Keep the branch-circuit drop under 3% and the total feeder plus branch drop under 5% at the calculated load.

title: Two small-appliance circuits
requirement: A kitchen needs at least two 20 A small-appliance branch circuits for the counter receptacles, and they may not feed anything else.

title: Laundry and bathroom circuits
requirement: A laundry needs its own 20 A circuit, and a bathroom receptacle needs a 20 A branch circuit that serves only bathroom receptacles.

title: Lighting outlets
requirement: Every habitable room, hallway, stairway, garage, outdoor entrance and basement needs a wall-switch-controlled lighting outlet.

title: Receptacle spacing
requirement: In a dwelling, no point along a wall may be more than 6 ft from a receptacle, so receptacles are at most 12 ft apart; kitchen counters need one within 24 in of every point.

title: Outdoor receptacle
requirement: A one- and two-family dwelling needs at least one outdoor receptacle at an accessible grade level, with a weatherproof in-use cover and GFCI protection.

title: GFCI protection
requirement: GFCI protection is required for dwelling receptacles in bathrooms, kitchens, garages, outdoors, crawl spaces, basements, laundry areas and within 6 ft of sinks.

title: AFCI protection
requirement: Branch circuits supplying outlets in dwelling living areas, bedrooms, hallways, closets, kitchens and laundry need arc-fault protection.

title: Grounding electrode system
requirement: All available grounding electrodes must be bonded into one grounding electrode system: a metal water pipe, a ground rod, a concrete-encased electrode and any other listed electrode.

title: Equipment grounding conductors
requirement: The equipment grounding conductor is sized from the overcurrent device: 14 AWG for 15 A, 12 for 20 A, 10 for 30–60 A, 8 for 100 A, 6 for 200 A, 4 for 300 A and 3 for 400 A.

title: Neutral demand load
requirement: The feeder neutral carries the maximum unbalanced load: 100% of the first 200 A of the line-to-neutral load and 70% of the remainder.

title: Range and dryer demand
requirement: An electric range takes the Table 220.55 demand for its rating, and a dryer takes 5,000 VA or the nameplate, whichever is larger.

title: Motor loads
requirement: Add 25% of the largest motor to the feeder load, and size the branch short-circuit protection from Table 430.52, which may be larger than the conductor ampacity.

title: EV charging
requirement: An EV branch circuit is sized at 125% of the charger’s maximum continuous current, needs GFCI protection, and the service calculation includes the charger at its full rating.

title: Pool and spa equipment circuits
requirement: Pool pump motors need GFCI protection, a disconnect within sight, and the equipotential bonding of Article 680.

title: Feeder to a detached building
requirement: A detached building takes one feeder, with a disconnecting means, a grounding electrode system and a separate ground bar at the remote panel.

title: What the inspector needs
requirement: A load calculation, a panel schedule with the directory, the service and feeder conductor sizes, the grounding electrode detail and the AFCI/GFCI listing.
